reuse.why: Routes the server midpoint copies through the existing exported getScheduledAmount and uses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance, but schedule-template.ts calls the sub-helpers with its own op dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: Removes the five inline midpoint calculations; what remains is a re-stated op dispatch in schedule-template.ts and a leftover null check in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the existing amount helper; the API field is computed in the existing scheduleModel.toExternal.

scope.why: Changing the pre-existing getScheduledAmount also changes UI consumers (SchedulesTable, Balance, useScheduleEdit range-to-number conversion) without acknowledgment, and three release notes are added for one combined change.

maintainability.why: Mostly one definition, but callers apply it unevenly (preview omits the op so approximate amounts are not worst-cased there, schedule-template dispatches itself), so the rule is not reliably 'changed once'.

bypasses_abstraction.where: budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList chooses between getRangedAmountWorstCase/getApproxAmountWorstCase itself instead of calling getScheduledAmount(value, false, op); computeSchedulePreviewTransactions calls getScheduledAmount without the op.

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template.ts re-expresses getScheduledAmount's number/range/approx dispatch as a nested ternary on amountCondition.op.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch; schedule-template.ts bypasses it with its own dispatch, and the preview in shared/schedules.ts calls it without op and keeps its own null guard.
